skill.name: tech-doc
skill.description: A writing guide for clear, bounded, and maintainable technical documentation in engineering collaboration.
skill.summary: Helps teams write structured technical docs, SOPs, references, and Markdown guides.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: The static command finding is a false positive because SKILL.md line 23 describes how to format shell examples in documentation. The entropy alert is also a false positive; the file is coherent Markdown text with Chinese content, not obfuscated or encrypted data. No prompt injection or malicious semantic intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - 代码块标注 `bash`/`sh`,无提示符,命令可直接复制执行;提供占位符说明,必要时给 `--dry-run` 或只读版本优先。

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (7.76 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 23 describes how documentation should label shell examples and prefer dry-run or read-only variants. It does not execute commands or instruct the assistant to run shell commands.
SKILL.md is plain Markdown with coherent Chinese instructions and front matter. The entropy score appears caused by Unicode text, not binary, encrypted, or hidden payload content.

content.value_statement: Technical teams lose time when docs mix assumptions, unclear scope, and hard-to-scan instructions. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce structured, cited, and maintainable technical documents.
actual_capabilities: Structures explanation documents around what, why, outcome, context, and reader needs.
Guides SOP and quick reference pages with scope, prerequisites, examples, and common errors.
Requires source boundaries, citations, versions, and access dates for key references.
Improves Markdown hierarchy, lists, code blocks, links, and image accessibility text.
Prompts collaboration when context is missing, assumptions are unclear, or risks need review.
limitations: Does not gather missing source material or verify facts without provided references.
Does not execute commands; it only guides how command examples should be written.
Does not replace expert review for regulated, safety-critical, or production change documents.
The source instructions are primarily Chinese, so localization preferences may need clarification.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn implementation notes into a scoped explanation with reader assumptions, outcomes, boundaries, and supporting evidence.

use_cases.title: Write Operational SOPs
use_cases.description: Build a concise procedure with prerequisites, risk notes, copyable examples, common errors, and related references.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Docs
use_cases.description: Define shared rules for Markdown structure, citations, terminology, command examples, and review handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Doc
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tech-doc skill to draft a short explanation document from these notes. State the goal, reader, scope, and outcome first.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite for Clarity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tech-doc skill to rewrite this document. Keep facts unchanged, reduce assumptions, tighten headings, and mark any missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Build an SOP
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tech-doc skill to create an SOP. Include scope, prerequisites, risk notes, shortest safe example, common errors, and references.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Documentation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tech-doc skill to review this technical document. Identify unsupported claims, unclear terms, missing citations, risky examples, and maintenance gaps.

output_examples.input: Rough notes describe a new caching feature and several edge cases.
output_examples.output: A reader-scoped explanation with a one-sentence conclusion, key behaviors, boundaries, examples, and a list of items needing confirmation.

output_examples.input: A team needs a repeatable deployment checklist from scattered chat notes.
output_examples.output: A concise SOP with prerequisites, risk warnings, the shortest safe path, common errors, and links to authoritative references.

output_examples.input: A Markdown guide has long sections, inconsistent terms, and weak citations.
output_examples.output: A cleaned document structure with shorter sections, consistent terminology, explicit citation gaps, and publication-ready formatting notes.

best_practices: Provide source notes, target reader, scope, and required terminology before asking for a draft.
Ask the assistant to mark uncertain facts instead of filling gaps from assumption.
Review command examples, permissions, and references before publishing operational documents.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent missing facts, metrics, or unsupported conclusions.
Do not publish command examples without reviewing permissions, placeholders, and dry-run options.
Do not mix tutorials, references, and SOPs without a clear reader goal.

faq.question: What kind of documents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports explanations, SOPs, quick references, Markdown guides, and team documentation standards.

faq.question: Can it verify whether technical facts are correct?
faq.answer: It can preserve and organize provided facts, but it needs trusted sources to verify claims.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands from the document?
faq.answer: No. It only gives writing guidance for safe and clear command examples.

faq.question: Can it help with API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure API explanations, define scope, standardize terms, and flag missing references.

faq.question: Is the skill suitable for multilingual teams?
faq.answer: Yes, but the source guidance is Chinese, so output language and terminology should be specified.

faq.question: How should I prepare input for best results?
faq.answer: Provide source notes, audience, goal, constraints, existing terminology, and any required references.
